findings.title: Mandatory destination Properties lack a specified YAML field encoding
findings.issue: The Drafts require Name and Path to be mandatory strings stored in frontmatter, but the successor maps the Properties generally to frontmatter and separately to Carrier filename/location without selecting YAML keys or a nested/flat structure. CA-D-478 Claim requires property names and canonical encodings registered by an applicable D policy rather than invented from a display path. D664 selects the frontmatter region but not the serialized field form.
findings.counterexample: Both carrier_destination.file.name/.path and flattened keys such as carrier_destination_file_name/_path can carry the same calculated values. The Drafts choose neither representation, so a writer has no Claim-level basis to select one canonical encoding.

evidence.excerpt: Name and Path are mandatory string Properties, stored in Atom frontmatter.
The generic non-Content-to-frontmatter mapping and Name/Path-to-filename/location mappings contain no YAML field-name or nesting encoding.

Details says a new field or nested key needs applicable authority for canonical location, type, cardinality, admission, and permitted-value/reference resolution. This stronger closure wording is not in the Claim.
Metadata belongs in YAML, using registered property names and canonical value encodings rather than a field invented from a display path.

findings.blast_radius: Leaves a writer or later migration without a selected canonical serialized form for the two fields. It does not alter any current Atom or existing filename/placement rule.
findings.minimal_fix: Add one explicit Delivery encoding for the two Property paths: exact YAML keys and nesting, scalar/string cardinality, and the calculation/agreement boundary. Do not change filename, placement, status, owner, Plan, or archive rules.
findings.confidence: high for the missing encoding; medium for any admission consequence because that depends on whether D657 Details are normative.
